thread:
Maya R: heads-up, I'm prototyping a slim variant preview for the model catalog. goal: quick glance for perf + version without cluttering rows. prototype: https://figma.redwood/variant-slim
Evan: love the clean look. two quick UX points: 1) too many badges make the compact preview feel noisy, 2) keyboard discoverability is low.
Tom: for badges can we show one primary (latency) and put the rest behind a small chevron that expands inline? keeps density low on hover.
Sam (a11y): a11y concerns: hover previews should not steal focus. use aria-live polite for announcements. make the chevron and "add to compare" control reachable by keyboard with clear aria-labels.
Maya R: agree. plan: hover -> aria-live announce; explicit open (Enter/Space) -> persistent overlay with tabbable controls. adding aria-labels like "Latency: 85 ms" for SRs.
Evan: animation note: overlay should avoid layout shifts. use position: absolute + transform for show/hide. also debounce aria-live updates ~400ms to avoid SR spam.
Tom: product ask: include a tiny "+ compare" checkbox in the overlay that maps to the compare table. makes multi-select flows faster.
Sam (a11y): test checklist I'll run: VoiceOver/NVDA announce on hover, keyboard flow to open overlay, add to compare via keyboard, and check no duplicate announcements when moving quickly.
DesignBot: snapshot created: branch feat/catalog/slim-preview (build 503).
Maya R: decision: ship keyboard & a11y behavior in patch; chevron collapse in next sprint. I'll update the figma and add microcopy changes (change badge tooltip to "Typical latency (p50)"). action items:
- Maya: update figma + prototype (EOD)
- Tom: implement overlay + debounce (PR by Tue)
- Sam: a11y test plan (after PR)
- Evan: microcopy edits + badge priority list

Maya R: small UX note: Esc should close the persistent overlay and return focus to the originating row. documented.
